QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_47

question.text: Within OECD DAC criteria, 'Efficiency' vs 'Effectiveness' — which pairing is correct?

answer.text: Efficiency = doing things right (input-to-output conversion, cost per beneficiary); Effectiveness = doing the right things (achieving the intended objectives)
Efficiency measures long-term impact; Effectiveness measures short-term output
Efficiency is qualitative; Effectiveness is quantitative

explanation.text: The Logic: Efficiency asks whether inputs are converted to outputs at the lowest cost and best timing — 'doing things right'. Effectiveness asks whether the intervention actually achieved its intended outcomes — 'doing the right things'. The two are complementary but distinct evaluation angles. The Trap: They are distinct, not synonyms. The time-horizon split is wrong. The qual/quant split is wrong. Cross-Exam Context: X-A IA, V-B MF Foundation and XV Research Analyst all distinguish efficiency and effectiveness for policy critique. XXIII expects the classic Drucker distinction. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Include cost-per-outcome metrics (INR per child vaccinated, INR per employment year) alongside outcome counts — efficiency ratios are often the single most investor-moving number in your AIR.
